report.summary: Reviewed transport.py chunk 1/1: all docstring claims kept; no defects or unreachable code found.

handoff.purpose: Define transport sink protocol and implementations for runtime-shell records.

symbols.name: TransportSink
symbols.note: Protocol with async publish method accepting TransportRecord.

symbols.name: InMemoryTransportSink
symbols.note: In-memory sink storing records in a list; deterministic for tests.

symbols.name: JsonlTransportSink
symbols.note: Append-only JSONL journal; uses asyncio lock and writes UTF-8.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink
symbols.note: Fans records out to multiple sinks; propagates failures.

claims.text: Persist or forward one lossless transport record.
claims.why: The protocol only declares the method signature; no implementation in this chunk to verify losslessness or persistence.

claims.text: Small deterministic sink for tests and embedded consumers.
claims.why: The sink simply appends records to a list in order; deterministic for tests.

claims.text: Append-only JSONL journal preserving every normalized input/output.
claims.why: Opens file in append mode ('a') and writes one line per record; preserves records. 'Normalized' is uncheckable here as it depends on TransportRecord.to_dict().

claims.text: Fan one record out to multiple sinks; failures remain visible.
claims.why: Iterates all sinks and awaits each publish; exceptions propagate, so failures are not swallowed.

observations.what: JsonlTransportSink uses asyncio.Lock but the file operations are synchronous (blocking) inside an async method; this may block the event loop but does not violate the docstring.

CompositeTransportSink does not attempt to continue after a sink failure; the docstring says 'failures remain visible' which is satisfied by propagation, but it does not explicitly state whether subsequent sinks are still called.
